あじゃず.name: Ajazu
あじゃず.desc: A stylish popular shop with jazz playing inside (is the name from Aja × jazz?). The entrance covered in greenery is the landmark, and the signature dish is the soki soba with three large pieces of soki on a light pork bone soup.
t: *I also had AI (Claude 3.5 sonnet) make this article, and I've edited and updated part of it myself lol
On my Okinawa soba tour, this time I'll introduce “Ajazu” in Akebono, Naha City! 😄 I ate here in September 2024 😄
I went to “Ajazu” in Akebono, Naha City. It's located heading toward the port from the Aja intersection on National Route 58.
The shop's exterior is really stylish! The sign reading “Okinawa Soba Ajazu” on the white wall catches the eye. There are lots of green plants around the entrance, full of tropical vibes 😊
Ajazu (the entrance is covered in green, so at a glance you can't tell (^0^;))
The sign for Ajazu's on-site parking lot
Ajazu entrance
When I entered the on-site parking lot, it was actually full (^0^;)
It was lunchtime, but I thought it must be a popular shop.
However, since it's Okinawa soba, I figured turnover would be quick and waited a bit on the premises. Then customers who had finished eating came out, and I somehow managed to park.

And when you go inside, jazz is playing as background music. I wonder if this is where the shop's name comes from? Maybe it's a pun on the place name “Aja” and “jazz.” It had a somewhat different atmosphere from other Okinawa soba shops, and felt a bit stylish.

Looking at the menu, besides the standard Okinawa soba, of course, there's also yushi-dofu (soft Okinawan tofu) soba and jushi (Okinawan seasoned rice). This time I went for the classic and ordered the “soki soba.”
The meal ticket machine near the entrance (this time I ordered soki soba)
While I waited, I looked around the shop, and maybe because it was lunchtime, it was really bustling. There were lots of locals too, and I felt that it's a popular shop.
Menu
Menu
Now, at last, the soki soba arrives! 🍜
Soki soba　¥880
First, the soup. Mmm, this is the standard pork bone base. It's light and easy to drink. It's just plain delicious, but I don't think it has a particularly standout personality.
Soki soba　¥880
Next, when I slurp the noodles, they're thin straight noodles and fairly soft. Personally, I thought they could have a little more chewiness / bite, but this might be where preferences differ.

Looking at the topping, the soki, there are three large pieces of soki on top! It seems to be one bone-in pork rib (hon-soki) and two soft-bone pork ribs (nankotsu soki). The seasoning is on the light side, so you can enjoy the flavor of the meat itself. However, there are some sinewy parts too.
Looking at it overall, “Ajazu's” soki soba doesn't do anything particularly unusual, but it's a stable taste.
But honestly, maybe because I saw how packed it was at lunchtime and expected too much, the taste was about “Yeah, just plain delicious.” It wasn't like I was especially moved! 😅

But Okinawa soba eaten in a shop with a nice atmosphere where jazz plays feels a little special just for that, doesn't it. If you've come to Naha sightseeing and want to enjoy Okinawa soba in a somewhat stylish atmosphere, I think “Ajazu” would be a good option.

Rating (9/15): Just plain delicious, but nothing particularly stands out; that's my impression. When you come to Akebono, Naha City, how about enjoying Okinawa soba in a somewhat stylish atmosphere at jazz-filled “Ajazu”? 😊 Now, which Okinawa soba shop should I go to next~. The Okinawa soba tour continues! Well then, look forward to next time~! 👋

The signature dish is the Kamezen soba with melt-in-your-mouth soft-bone pork ribs (nankotsu soki) in a light soup fragrant with bonito.

This time I ordered the “Kamezen soba,” which bears the shop's name, without hesitation. The bowl brought out had a clear, golden soup with thin wavy noodles. And on top, thin strips of yellow omelet and a large soft-bone pork rib (nankotsu soki) sit there boldly. It looks simple, but it's the classic Okinawa soba style.

Kamezen soba　¥980

Sunagawa Seimenjo
The shop's exterior has a stylish feel, and photos of the signature menu items were displayed near the entrance. Just looking at that sign conveys that the soup seems good 😊

Looking at the menu, there are various kinds of Okinawa soba, and I decided to order the “special soba,” which was marked as recommended. The menu description says the broth is carefully made from ingredients such as bonito, kombu, dried sardines, mackerel, scallops, and chicken. This looks promising 🤗
Inside the shop (there are no walls, so it's practically outside 😄)

北谷そば.name: Chatan Soba
北谷そば.desc: A popular shop that uses Chatan salt (100% seawater from off the Miyagi coast). The wall covered in autograph boards is overwhelming, and the signature dish is the seared salt nankotsu soba. You can choose from medium-flat noodles or wavy noodles.
t: This time my Okinawa soba tour took me to “Chatan Soba” in Kuwae, Chatan Town 🍜　I ate here in March 2025 😄
Chatan Soba
Chatan Soba
Chatan Soba

The exterior is a bit unique; it's in a corner of an apartment building, so to speak, with the shop's name written big on the wooden enclosure below the building. White stones are laid around the entrance, along with wooden decorations and handwritten signs, and the contrast with the concrete feel outside was interesting. There was also a notice for the “tofu soba,” limited to 10 servings, and this kind of handmade-feeling presentation felt somehow friendly 😊
Celebrity autographs posted on the wall
Celebrity autographs posted on the wall
Celebrity autographs posted on the wall
Celebrity autographs posted on the wall
Celebrity autographs posted on the wall
Inside the shop
Inside the shop

When you go inside, this is quite distinctive too: autograph boards are lined up across an entire wall, making a strong impact. There were autographs from players of the Kings and the Chunichi Dragons too, a space where you immediately understand, “Ah, this place is pretty famous.” There are also tatami seats with the warmth of wood, and including the lighting and decorations, it had a calm, Okinawan atmosphere overall, and I felt that rather than being aimed at tourists, it must be a shop properly loved by local customers too. However, there were actually lots of local customers and it seems quite popular, so on this day I waited a fair while. Moreover, even after being shown to my seat, the food didn't come out quickly from there, and overall the wait was on the long side. Even if not as long as at Jagaru Soba, it might feel a bit long to impatient people (^0^;)
Menu
Chatan Soba's explanation panel
Menu

Looking at the menu, there were Okinawa soba, soki soba, salt nankotsu soba, mixed soba, and so on, and the way they push Chatan salt was memorable too. There was also a notice that they use “Chatan salt” made from 100% seawater from off the Miyagi coast in Chatan Town, which clearly conveyed their commitment to ingredients. This time I ordered the recommended “seared salt nankotsu soba,” and since I could choose the noodles from medium-flat noodles or wavy noodles, I chose the wavy noodles, which were also recommended. Being able to choose your own noodles is a nice little point.
Seared salt nankotsu soba, large　¥900

The bowl that was brought out looked fairly simple. In a clear soup sat seared soft-bone pork ribs (nankotsu soki), with green onions and omelet alongside. When I first drank the soup, it was pork-bone-based, yet the salt came clearly to the front. As you'd expect from using Chatan salt, it has personality, but personally I felt the saltiness was a bit strong. It's a light type, but rather than gently and slowly soaking in, it was a type of soup that pretty clearly tells you, “The salt is coming through.”
Seared salt nankotsu soba, large　¥900
The medium-thin wavy noodles I chose were on the soft side in texture, and people who want to fully enjoy firmness might find them a bit lacking.

The seared salt soft-bone pork ribs (nankotsu soki) have a browned look that whets the appetite, and when I actually ate them, overall they leaned light, with a melt-in-your-mouth tenderness too. However, depending on the part, there were places where a sinewy texture clearly remained, so not all of it was the melting type. I thought the toastiness of the searing would come forward more, but that was surprisingly modest, and my impression was that, for better or worse, it came together safely. The composition of the toppings is simple too, so rather than focusing on impact, it's a calm bowl.

Looking at it as a whole, it was a shop with lots of intriguing elements, like the shop's atmosphere, the commitment to ingredients, its local popularity, and the number of autographs, and I think it actually has an appeal that makes you want to try it once. However, speaking honestly as Anji, compared with how my expectations rose, including the wait, the taste landed at “ordinary.” I didn't feel a strong deciding factor like “I want to come back to eat this again!”

Rating (9/15): It seems to be a popular shop, but my honest impression was that the taste is just plain delicious, I guess~. It's worth experiencing once including the atmosphere, but the decisive factor that makes you want to come back is weak; that's the kind of bowl it was 🙂

まるち 北谷店.name: Maruchi Chatan-ten
まるち 北谷店.desc: Maruchi's third shop, marked by white Ryukyu roof tiles and a shisa. So popular a line forms right at opening; the customization of 3 soups × 3 noodles is the same, and there's also bone-in pork rib (hon-soki) soba exclusive to the Chatan branch. Lunch comes with complimentary jushi (Okinawan seasoned rice).
t: On my Okinawa soba tour, this time I visited “Maruchi Chatan-ten,” an Okinawa soba specialty shop in Yoshihara, Chatan Town 🍜　I ate here in March 2025 😄
Maruchi Chatan-ten
My first encounter with “Maruchi” was the Maruchi Nakagusuku branch, and after that I also visited the Nanjo City Tsukishiro branch, so this time is actually my visit to a third branch.
*By the way, this is the Maruchi Nakagusuku branch (I ate there in January 2024 lol)
*By the way, this is the Maruchi Nanjo City Tsukishiro branch (I ate there in July 2024 lol)
The Nakagusuku branch and the Nanjo City branch were both popular, and this Chatan branch is no exception: customers were lining up in droves right at opening 😲
Maruchi Chatan-ten (a line right at opening lol)
Maruchi Chatan-ten (a line right at opening lol)
Maruchi Chatan-ten (a line right at opening lol)
Maybe because it's in Chatan Town, an area with lots of tourists, it seems to draw a wide range of customers from locals to tourists, and I was reminded again of how popular the Maruchi brand is.

On the exterior, the roof of white Ryukyu tiles, so typical of Okinawa, stands out against the blue sky, and a shisa welcomes you from on top of the roof 🦁　Not only inside, but picnic tables are also lined up outdoors on the gravel, and on a nice day it looks pleasant to eat outside ✨　It's an old-folk-house-style building, but the inside has been neatly renovated, and it gave a calm yet clean impression.
You can eat outdoors too 😄

Now, looking at the menu, a big feature of Maruchi is the system where you can choose the soup and the noodles each from 3 kinds. The soup is a choice of 3: “light soup (our secret recipe),” “rich soup (our pride),” and “salt soup (simple is best).” My experience with the light soup at the Nakagusuku branch had stuck in my memory, so this time I tried choosing the “rich soup” 💪　It's apparently a rich preparation made by simmering prefectural chicken and pork bone for a long time, which raises my expectations 🤤　You can choose the noodles from “thin noodles,” “flat noodles,” and “wavy noodles,” and this time I went with the staff's recommendation and chose “wavy noodles.”
Explanation of the 3 soups
Explanation of the 3 noodles
Menu
Menu
Menu

What I ordered this time was the Chatan-branch-exclusive menu item “bone-in pork rib (hon-soki) soba (large) ¥980.” It coming with the lunchtime-service jushi (Okinawan seasoned rice) was a nice point too 🍚
Bone-in pork rib (hon-soki) soba, large　¥980 (jushi (Okinawan seasoned rice) free)

Facing the bowl that was brought out, first a sip of the soup. As expected of the rich type, the chicken and pork bone broth flavor is solid. However, the saltiness is a bit strong, and I got a somewhat different impression from the creamy, mellow smoothness of the pork-bone-based soups at Nankuru, Uehara Soba, and Tsukikuroki. Rather than a deep umami, the salt comes to the front 🤔
Bone-in pork rib (hon-soki) soba, large　¥980
As for the wavy noodles, they're a medium-thick type with a moderate chewiness, and they cling to the soup quite well too 😊

The topping, the bone-in pork ribs (hon-soki), are well simmered and melt-in-your-mouth tender overall, but depending on the part, there were places where a sinewy texture remained, giving the impression of a mix of tender parts and parts with a solid meaty feel 😄　And the jushi (Okinawan seasoned rice) that came as a lunchtime-only service is a delight! The combination of Okinawa soba and jushi (Okinawan seasoned rice) really is the best ✨

Rating (9/15): Comparing Maruchi's three branches, the Nakagusuku branch, the Nanjo City Tsukishiro branch, and the Chatan branch, you can see they all have steady popularity. The atmosphere created by making use of old folk houses and the high degree of customization, where you can choose the soup and noodles, must be what attracts so many customers. The taste is “just plain delicious,” and my impression is that rather than having a standout personality, it's an Okinawa soba you can eat with peace of mind. Even so, I think the brand power that creates a line right after opening is the real thing ✨

三色屋.name: Sanshoku-ya
三色屋.desc: An Okinawa soba specialty shop with the motto “to become number one in Ginowan.” Its pride is soup you can choose from 3 kinds (chicken, pork, or blend), house-made fresh noodles, and melt-in-your-mouth seared soki served on a separate plate. Changing up the flavor with bonito oil is fun too.
t: ― 2nd Visit (October 2024) ―
*This article was created with AI (Claude 3.5 Sonnet), with parts edited and updated by me 😆
I went to eat here in October 2024 😁😊　This time I'll introduce “Sanshoku-ya” in Aichi, Ginowan City. This shop is a participating shop in the 14th Okinawa Soba Stamp Rally, and this is my 2nd visit.
Sanshoku-ya
Sanshoku-ya

The shop is on the 1st floor of a reddish-brown building, and the white noren (shop curtain) is the landmark 😄　There's a handwritten sign at the entrance, with a notice that the “extra-large seared soki” is sold out. It must be a popular menu item.
The “extra-large seared soki” introduced in the stamp rally booklet was sold out (^0^;)　Too bad 😆
Inside the shop
The interior has a retro atmosphere, with red sofa seats and counter seats. Brick-style tiles are used on the walls, giving it a calm atmosphere 🏮
Menu
Menu

Looking at the menu, standard Okinawa soba items like “braised pork belly (sanmai-niku) soba” and “seared soki soba” are all there. And what's distinctive is that you can choose the soup from 3 kinds (chicken broth, pork broth, blend). Last time I chose chicken broth, so this time I tried ordering the “seared soki soba” with pork broth.
Seared soki soba　¥900

The Okinawa soba that was brought out after a while has a striking clear soup. First, a sip of the soup. A smooth, pork-bone-based mouthfeel, and I can feel a deep taste a cut above other shops. The depth of the soup is wonderful 😋　However, I also feel the saltiness is a bit strong.

The noodles are medium-thick with a gentle wave, and apparently they use house-made fresh noodles. Along with a chewy texture, they cling to the soup excellently. You can taste the flavor unique to fresh noodles too, and they're delicious 🍜

The topping, the seared soki, is served on a separate plate, a trick to keep its flavor from transferring to the soup. It's simmered melt-in-your-mouth tender, searing adds toastiness, and it's very satisfying to eat. Partway through, when I added the shop's original bonito oil to the soup, I could enjoy a different, deep taste.

Rating (12/15): A wonderful Okinawa soba where every element is finished at a high level. The soup especially has a deep taste with concentrated pork bone umami, and it goes perfectly with the noodles. The balance of the seared soki's tenderness and toastiness is exquisite too. The idea of letting you enjoy a flavor change with the original bonito oil is wonderful. When you come to Ginowan City, how about dropping by? 😊
― 1st Visit (July 2024) ―

I went to eat here in July 2024 😁

This time I'll introduce “Sanshoku-ya” in Aichi, Ginowan City. On my journey touring Okinawa soba shops on the main island of Okinawa, I've visited quite a number of shops, but I'm still far from conquering them all. But I'll do my best, one shop at a time, aiming to conquer them all lol
Sanshoku-ya

Now, “Sanshoku-ya,” which I visited this time. Actually, it's a shop I'd been curious about for a while. Why? Because of the words on the sign that catches my eye every time I pass along National Route 330. I'd been drawn in by the catchphrase “Okinawa soba that will become number one in Ginowan,” which is just overflowing with confidence.
Sanshoku-ya's sign along National Route 330 (whether it's modest or overflowing with confidence, it's catchy and eye-catching 😆)
When you turn onto the road with the sign from National Route 330, the shop is right there. There was also a dedicated parking lot diagonally across.
When you turn in from National Route 330, the shop is on the left, and this parking lot is on the right, diagonally across
When you go inside, there are counter seats and table seats; the interior is built like a former snack bar. (Sorry, I didn't take photos)

Looking at the menu, besides Okinawa soba, there are also a few rice dish items. But the purpose this time was, of course, “Okinawa soba that will become number one in Ginowan.” So I decided to order the signature Okinawa soba.

Menu (an unusual one)

When ordering, I learned that you can choose the soup. You can choose from 3 kinds: chicken broth, pork broth, or blend. When I asked the staff, they said the most popular is chicken broth. So this time I tried choosing chicken broth.
While I was looking for a while at the menu, which even includes the profile of a manager who seems to have quite a character? (lol), the Okinawa soba I ordered was brought out.
Okinawa soba that will become number one in Ginowan　¥1,400

First, the soup. When I take a sip... oh, this is unexpected! It's a slightly different taste from other Okinawa soba shops. Maybe because it's based on chicken broth, I sense a taste somewhat close to ramen soup. But it's unmistakably the taste of Okinawa soba. Rich and mellow. Preferences might be divided on this, but personally it was a taste I liked a lot.

Next, I have the noodles. A chewy texture is their characteristic. They have chewiness / bite too and cling well to the soup. I have the impression that many Okinawa soba noodles are on the soft side, but the noodles here have a moderate springiness and are very satisfying to eat. Delicious.

Pay attention to the toppings too. The seared soft-bone pork ribs (nankotsu soki) were especially memorable. A tender texture that falls apart. A deliciousness that melts in your mouth. Besides the regular seared soft-bone pork ribs (nankotsu soki), there was also salt-seared soki.

According to the profile of the owner, Mr. Ishikawa, on the menu, he also trained at the famous Okinawa soba shops “Chinchiki Soba” and “Ishigufu.” I see, now that you mention it, there's something similar in the taste, I thought, convinced.

According to Mr. Ishikawa, in July 2023 he temporarily closed Sanshoku-ya (at the time, Sanshokudon-ya), and reopened it renewed in 2024. At that time, he's also taking on the challenge of making noodles using house-made wheat. A story where you truly feel his passion for Okinawa soba.

Rating (12/15): Even while the owner says he's raising the bar, I felt he must also have a fair amount of confidence. No lie in the catchphrase “Okinawa soba that will become number one in Ginowan”! Preferences may vary by person, but I thought it might be the most delicious of the Okinawa soba shops in Ginowan City I've eaten at so far~. How about trying it once? It's recommended 😄
